name: libdill
listed_description: Library which makes structured concurrent programming (awesome-c, Concurrency and Parallelism)
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline. README points to libdill.org; the repo's own faq.html says only 'The best way to find out is to check for yourself' and structured-concurrency.html says switching is 'extremely fast. It requires only a few machine instructions' (directional, no numbers). perf/ holds chan.c, choose.c, ctxswitch.c, done.c, go.c, timer.c and whispers.c, which time libdill alone and compare to nothing. Third-party searches found no libdill row in a coroutine shootout (libco, libaco, Boost.Context searches returned none; the '50 million context switches per second' figure belongs to libmill). libdill.org itself is EGRESS_BLOCKED. MIT, 1.9k stars; suggested category coroutines-fibers (runtime-and-systems), not concurrency-queues-locks.

name: libdjb
listed_description: Collection of libraries doing various things. (Apparently) public domain. (awesome-c, Source Code Collections)
reason: No evidence reachable. www.fefe.de is EGRESS_BLOCKED, so the page could not be opened. The listing describes a source collection of djb-style libraries with no performance claim, and no benchmark or comparison naming libdjb was found. It has no single component identified with a baseline.

name: libenvpp
listed_description: A modern C++ library for type-safe environment variable parsing. (awesome-cpp, Miscellaneous)
reason: No performance claim anywhere. README (25 KB) has no benchmark, speed or comparison text; repo root has no benchmark directory (.github/workflows, cmake, cmake_integration_test, examples, external, include/libenvpp, source, test). Apache-2.0, 172 stars; it is a type-safe environment-variable parser (no meaningful speed baseline), not serialization-json.

name: libgcrypt
listed_description: General-purpose cryptography library, with a range of algorithms (awesome-c, Crypto)
reason: No reachable numeric comparison against an external baseline. Reachable evidence (github.com/gpg/libgcrypt NEWS, raw file) lists only speedups of libgcrypt over its own earlier releases (for example AES-XTS 6 times faster, SHA-1/SHA-256 4.0/3.7 times faster with Intel SHA extensions, SHA-512 4.5 times faster on Ryzen 7). Reachable jkivilin/bench-slopes README (OpenSSL, Nettle, Botan, Crypto++, libgcrypt) prints example outputs from different machines and library versions, not a head-to-head. Two candidate comparisons exist but their pages are EGRESS_BLOCKED, so only WebSearch summaries were seen and nothing was verified: (1) gnupg.org/blog/20131215-gcrypt-bench.html 'Speedups in Libgcrypt 1.6' (summary: libgcrypt 1.6 reaches top speed of all compared implementations for SHA-1, SHA-256/512 improved, AES throughput well above 1.5 and considerably above Nettle); (2) a 2018 nettle-bugs mailing-list message on lists.lysator.liu.se (summary: AES-128-CBC on a Core i7-6820HQ with Fedora 26 packages: nettle-3.3 850 MB/s, libgcrypt-1.7.8 1172 MB/s, gnutls-3.5.14 1230 MB/s, openssl-1.1.0f 1153 MB/s; libgcrypt only 1.7% above OpenSSL). Retry both from an environment that can open them. Suggested category aead-and-ciphers (crypto-and-hashing), not concurrency-queues-locks; LGPL-2.1+.

name: libgd
listed_description: Library for the dynamic creation of images by programmers (awesome-cpp Image Processing; awesome-c Graphics)
reason: No project speed claim; README, CHANGELOG and docs have no benchmark text. The only numbers are third-party and mostly unfavourable: github.com/libvips/libvips/wiki/Speed-and-memory-use (libvips author's vips-bench, AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3955WX, Ubuntu 25.04, run 12 Aug 2025, JPEG crop+shrink+sharpen of a 10000x10000 image, best of five) lists jpg-gd (libgd 2.3.3) at 5.47 s, 761.68 MB peak, 6.67x slower than libvips (vips-c 8.18, 0.57 s). libgd is slower than convert 4.44 s, magick 4.41 s, gm 2.05 s, pillow-simd 1.51 s, OpenCV 3.15 s and imlib2 3.43 s, and faster only than pnm (netpbm) 6.06 s, PHP imagick 10.53 s, gmic 11.63 s and octave 35.1 s; the page notes libgd could not read TIFF so JPEG input was used. That is a non-claim by a rival project, so no record was written; a later pass may add it as a keep-and-document entry if wanted. MIT. Suggested category image-codecs or rasterizers-2d (media-and-graphics), not small-buffer-and-strings.

name: libgeohash
listed_description: Pure C implementation of the Geohash algorithm. (awesome-c, Utilities)
reason: No numeric comparison. Repo (BSD-3-Clause, 111 stars, 21 commits, authored by Derek Smith) has only a geohash_test.c correctness test and no README benchmark. raw.githubusercontent.com README.md returned 404. A WebSearch for geohash benchmarks surfaced a Python package also named libgeohash and .NET geohash libraries (NetGeohash and others), which are different projects. Suggested category geometry-spatial (numerics-and-science).
